subject: Clarify maintenance carve-outs and SLA credit triggers for Order Form
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Emma Shaw <emma@starlite.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — maintenance carve-outs

Emma — thanks for sending the marked Order Form. We reviewed the maintenance carve-outs and the credit trigger language and want to propose a more operationally predictable approach so both sides have clear expectations. High level thoughts: 

- Scheduled maintenance: we'll keep the 8-hour rolling blackout per calendar week cap but propose defining "scheduled maintenance" as announced >72 hours in advance and limited to a maximum of 4 hours per maintenance window during business hours. That keeps planned work small and predictable.

- Emergency maintenance: we agree to minimize these; propose they be limited to critical security fixes. We will log and notify with attempted comms within 1 hour. Emergency events should not count toward SLA credits unless they exceed a 4-hour contiguous outage and we determine the customer-facing service was impacted.

- Credit triggers: rather than a single uptime % threshold that can be brittle with transient infra behavior, we propose a tiered credit table with a 30-minute exclusion window for blips under 2 minutes (to avoid noisy retries). See attached "maintenance-carveouts-v1.xlsx" for example calculations.

Can your procurement team accept narrower scheduled windows, or do you need us to keep a broader blackout for operational flexibility? I copied Lauren and Kim to get vendor-legal input before I send a consolidated counterproposal.

Attachments: maintenance-carveouts-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet with examples)

Thanks,
Diego
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Emma Shaw <emma@starlite.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: Starlite Procurement <procurement@starlite.ai>, ops-legal@starlite.ai
Date: 2028-11-20T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — maintenance carve-outs

Diego — appreciate the quick read. A few clarifications from our side before legal weighs in: 

- Starlite is willing to accept scheduled windows announced >72 hrs in advance but needs at least one 8-hour blackout per month outside of business hours for major upgrades (we can't agree to multiple small windows that increase release risk).

- For emergency maintenance we need explicit definitions and an audit trail requirement (ticket + timeline) to validate whether a credit should be issued.

- Regarding the 30-minute exclusion for "blips": procurement prefers a slightly longer smoothing window of 5 minutes to account for transient network flaps.

I've attached our redline of the Order Form (OrderForm-Starlite-markup.pdf). Procurement would also like example credit math showing how credits map to monthly invoices — that will make approvals faster.

Thanks,
Emma
Director of Procurement
Starlite AI
Attachments: OrderForm-Starlite-markup.pdf

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-20T11:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — maintenance carve-outs

Diego / team — looping legal & pricing. Quick notes from Product / Sales ops after reading Emma's markup: 

- We should not commit to an "8-hour blackout per month outside business hours" as a guaranteed window; instead offer a single monthly 8-hour outside-business-hours maintenance window with option for an additional window by mutual agreement. That preserves operational agility while giving Starlite predictability.

- For emergency maintenance: Kimberly, we need a short, enforceable definition and a requirement for Redwood to provide the audit trail within 72 hours after the event. Starlite asked for tighter auditability — reasonable.

- Blip smoothing: from cost and reliability POV we prefer 2 minutes (keeps credit risk low). If procurement insists on 5 minutes, we can agree to 5 minutes but only for network-layer transient events, not for degraded throughput or partial feature failures. We should codify categories (network blip vs. platform outage).

Diego: I drafted suggested clause language in the attached credit examples worksheet. If you want, I can reframe into a one-pager that legal can sign off on.

—Lauren
Director, Revenue Operations

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Emma Shaw <emma@starlite.ai>, Starlite Procurement <procurement@starlite.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-20T14:38:00-08:00
Subject: Consolidated counterproposal and example credit math (please review)

Emma / team — thanks for the clear asks. Attached is our consolidated counterproposal and an example credit worksheet that maps uptime buckets to invoice credits. Summary of changes: 

1) Scheduled maintenance: Redwood proposes one guaranteed 8-hour outside-business maintenance window per calendar month; additional scheduled windows require mutual agreement and 72-hour notice. We will provide a monthly maintenance calendar by the 5th of each month.

2) Emergency maintenance: defined as "maintenance required to remediate critical security vulnerabilities or to prevent imminent systemic failure as determined by Redwood engineering." We will provide an incident ticket and timeline within 48 hours after the emergency event. Credits will only be considered if the event results in a customer-facing outage >4 contiguous hours.

3) Blip smoothing/exclusions: 2-minute exclusion for transient network flaps; 5-minute smoothing allowed for network-only incidents subject to agreed categorization.

4) Credit table: tiered credits (0.5% for monthly uptime <99.9% but >=99.5%, 1.5% for <99.5% but >=99.0%, 5% for <99.0%). See "credit-examples-worksheet.csv" for three invoice scenarios.

Kimberly — can legal review the emergency definition and the 48-hour audit turnaround? If acceptable we can prepare a tracked-redline to the Order Form and attach to DocuSign.

Attachments: credit-examples-worksheet.csv (3 scenarios), consolidated-counterproposal.pdf (summary)

Next steps requested: 
- Starlite: confirm whether the single monthly 8-hour window is acceptable or if you require the alternate phrasing Emma suggested.
- Kim: legal review on emergency definition + audit SLA.

Thanks — I can move to a tracked-redline once we have legal alignment.
Diego

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Emma Shaw <emma@starlite.ai>, Starlite Procurement <procurement@starlite.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-21T16:24:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Consolidated counterproposal and example credit math (legal review)

Diego / Emma — legal has reviewed the counterproposal. Two small but important edits from a compliance/risk standpoint: 

1) Emergency maintenance definition: accept with one edit — replace "as determined by Redwood engineering" with "as reasonably determined by Redwood, acting in good faith, and documented with incident rationale." This gives us some operational flexibility while giving Starlite a basis to challenge if needed.

2) Audit turnaround: we can commit to providing incident documentation within 72 hours (not 48). Operations needs that wiggle room to collect logs and post-mortem notes.

Also, we will include a carveout that scheduled maintenance for customer-requested one-off work (e.g., data migration requested by Starlite) is excluded from credit calculations when mutually scheduled.

If Starlite is comfortable with those two edits, legal can prepare a tracked-redline and we can push to DocuSign the same day. I copied Lauren for pricing confirmation and Rishi for signoff on the credit tiers.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
Attachments: (none)
